answer: The terrace multiplier is published, charged in lantern, and vine lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4836 identities would post 941 proofs and burn roughly 14 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
